newsitem.title: GERMANY: SGL Carbon denies involved in pricing cartel.
newsitem.headline: SGL Carbon denies involved in pricing cartel.

text.p: Germany's SGL Carbon, under investigation by U.S. and European Union officials, denied on Friday it was part of a price-fixing cartel and said no concrete charges had been made against the group.
"There have been no concrete accusations by the cartel authorities against SGL Carbon," a group spokesman told Reuters in response to an enquiry.

SGL Carbon said on Thursday that its offices in the United States and Germany had been searched as part of a possible price-fixing scheme in the graphite electrodes industry. The electrodes are used in steelmaking.
SGL Carbon, along with Carbide/Graphite Group Inc and UCAR International Inc, said their records had been subpoenaed by authorities, including the European Union.
"We have laid everything open," the SGL Carbon spokesman said. "We have nothing to hide. SGL has not engaged in any illegal price-fixing activities."
He said a search of the company's headquarters by the authorities would be completed today.
SGL Carbon's shares had slumped 8.65 percent to 237.70 marks in early bourse trade on news of the probe but recovered to trade higher at 241 marks in post-bourse electronic trade.
